questions.q: Why can a plain `RESTORE DATABASE` fail when restoring to a different server?
options: The backup contains the exact physical file paths from the source server, and the target server may not have those same drives or folders
Cross-server restores are blocked by SQL Server licensing
RESTORE DATABASE requires the target server to have less storage than the source
Backups can only ever be restored on the exact same physical machine
questions.explain: A backup bakes in the original physical file paths; if the target server's drive layout differs, SQL Server can't recreate the files there without help.

questions.q: What does the `MOVE` clause reference for each file — the physical path or the logical name?
options: The database's display name in SSMS
The physical path from the original server
The logical name, which RESTORE FILELISTONLY reveals
The backup file's own filename
questions.explain: MOVE takes a logical file name (discoverable via RESTORE FILELISTONLY) and maps it to a new physical path on the target server.

questions.q: Why do database users commonly become "orphaned" after restoring a database to a new server?
options: Orphaned users only happen when RECOVERY is omitted
Database users move with the restored database, but SQL Server logins are server-level objects that don't automatically exist on the new server
SQL Server deletes all users during any cross-server restore
Orphaned users are caused by using MOVE incorrectly
questions.explain: The user object travels with the database, but the login it's mapped to is a separate, server-level object that has to be recreated or matched on the target server.

options: Immediately deletes all orphaned users
Detects orphaned database users on the current database
Creates a brand-new database from the backup
Moves data and log files to new physical paths
questions.explain: Run in Report mode, sp_change_users_login lists orphaned users so they can be reviewed and then repaired.

questions.q: A production backup restores successfully onto a staging server using MOVE, but an application account that worked in production can't log in on staging. What is the most likely cause?
options: RESTORE FILELISTONLY was never run before the restore
The backup itself is corrupted
The MOVE clause was used incorrectly and corrupted the data file
The database user is orphaned because there's no matching login (with the same SID) on the staging server
questions.explain: This is the classic orphaned-user scenario — the database-level user restored fine, but the server-level login it depends on doesn't exist on staging.
